examples.question_text: Find the stationary point of $y=2x^{2}-12x+7$ and classify it using the second derivative.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}y'&=4x-12\\4x-12&=0\\x&=3\\y(3)&=18-36+7=-11\\y''&=4>0\end{aligned}$
The stationary point $(3,-11)$ is a local minimum.

examples.question_text: Find and classify the stationary points of $f(x)=2x^{3}-9x^{2}-24x+6$ using the second derivative.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=6x^{2}-18x-24\\&=6(x-4)(x+1)\end{aligned}$
For stationary points:
$\begin{aligned}6(x-4)(x+1)&=0\\x&=-1,\ 4\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}f(-1)&=-2-9+24+6=19\\f(4)&=128-144-96+6=-106\\f''(x)&=12x-18\\f''(-1)&=-30<0\\f''(4)&=30>0\end{aligned}$
Local maximum at $(-1,19)$; local minimum at $(4,-106)$.

examples.question_text: Find and classify all stationary points of $f(x)=x^{4}-8x^{2}+5$ using the second derivative.
Find and classify the stationary points of $f(x)=(x-2)^{2}(x+4)$ using the second derivative.
examples.solution_text:
Use the product rule:
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=2(x-2)(x+4)+(x-2)^{2}\\&=(x-2)(2x+8+x-2)\\&=3(x-2)(x+2)\end{aligned}$
For stationary points:
$\begin{aligned}3(x-2)(x+2)&=0\\x&=-2,\ 2\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}f(-2)&=(-4)^{2}(2)=32\\f(2)&=0\\f'(x)&=3x^{2}-12\\f''(x)&=6x\\f''(-2)&=-12<0\\f''(2)&=12>0\end{aligned}$
Local maximum at $(-2,32)$; local minimum at $(2,0)$.

examples.question_text: The curve $y=ax^{2}-8x+3$ has a stationary point at $x=2$. Find $a$, then find and classify that stationary point.
examples.solution_text:
$y'=2ax-8$.
Since $y'(2)=0$:
$\begin{aligned}4a-8&=0\\a&=2\end{aligned}$
Substitute into the function:
$\begin{aligned}y&=2x^{2}-8x+3\\y(2)&=8-16+3=-5\\y''&=4>0\end{aligned}$
The stationary point $(2,-5)$ is a local minimum.

examples.question_text: Find and classify the stationary points of $y=3x+\dfrac{48}{x}$, where $x\ne0$, using the second derivative.
examples.solution_text:
$y'=3-\dfrac{48}{x^{2}}$.
For stationary points:
$\begin{aligned}3-\frac{48}{x^{2}}&=0\\3x^{2}&=48\\x^{2}&=16\\x&=\pm4\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}y(-4)&=-12-12=-24\\y(4)&=12+12=24\\y''&=\frac{96}{x^{3}}\end{aligned}$
At $x=-4$, $y''=-\dfrac32<0$, so $(-4,-24)$ is a local maximum.
At $x=4$, $y''=\dfrac32>0$, so $(4,24)$ is a local minimum.

examples.question_text: For $f(x)=3x^{3}+4$ and $g(x)=2x^{4}-3$, find each stationary point. Show that the second-derivative test is inconclusive, then use a slope table to classify each point.
examples.solution_text:
For $f$:
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=9x^{2}\\9x^{2}&=0\\x&=0\\f(0)&=4\\f''(x)&=18x\\f''(0)&=0\end{aligned}$
The second-derivative test is inconclusive.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&-1&0&1\\\hline f'(x)&9&0&9\\\text{sign}&+&0&+\end{array}$
Since $f'(x)>0$ on both sides, $(0,4)$ is a horizontal point of inflection. Also, $f''(x)=18x$ changes from negative to positive there.
For $g$:
$\begin{aligned}g'(x)&=8x^{3}\\8x^{3}&=0\\x&=0\\g(0)&=-3\\g''(x)&=24x^{2}\\g''(0)&=0\end{aligned}$
The second-derivative test is inconclusive.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&-1&0&1\\\hline g'(x)&-8&0&8\\\text{sign}&-&0&+\end{array}$
The gradient changes from negative to positive, so $(0,-3)$ is a local minimum.

examples.question_text: Find and classify every stationary point of $f(x)=x^{4}-8x^{3}+2$. Use a slope table wherever the second-derivative test fails.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=4x^{3}-24x^{2}\\&=4x^{2}(x-6)\end{aligned}$
For stationary points:
$\begin{aligned}4x^{2}(x-6)&=0\\x&=0,\ 6\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}f(0)&=2\\f(6)&=1296-1728+2=-430\\f''(x)&=12x^{2}-48x\\f''(6)&=144>0\end{aligned}$
Local minimum at $(6,-430)$.
Since $f''(0)=0$, use a slope table at $x=0$:
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&-1&0&1\\\hline f'(x)&-28&0&-20\\\text{sign}&-&0&-\end{array}$
The gradient is negative on both sides. Also, $f''(x)=12x(x-4)$ changes from positive to negative at $x=0$, confirming a horizontal point of inflection at $(0,2)$.
